headline: Braves Bludgeon Red Sox Bullpen In Brutal Ten To Two Loss At Fenway
morning_brew: Just one day after Connelly Early gave us a reason to smile, the Red Sox pitching staff completely imploded at Fenway Park. Atlanta handed us a brutal ten to two loss, showing just how fragile this team really is right now. Payton Tolle battled hard on the mound for four and two-thirds innings, striking out seven batters and only giving up two earned runs. But once the bullpen took over, the wheels came off in absolute fashion. Greg Weissert and Ryan Watson combined to give up four earned runs in their relief appearances, turning a tight game into a complete laugher by the time the ninth inning wrapped up.

The bats could not bail out the pitching either, managing only eight hits against a tough Atlanta pitching staff. Willson Contreras and Wilyer Abreu each picked up a hit, but there was zero clutch hitting when we needed to spark a rally. This loss drops us to twenty-three and thirty-two on the season, keeping us dead last in the division. Numbers don't lie, the eye test agrees, this roster just does not have the depth to compete with the top tier of baseball. Now the Sox head out to Cleveland to face a first-place Guardians team that is sitting at thirty-three and twenty-five. If we do not find some consistency on the mound, this upcoming road trip is going to be incredibly painful to watch.

Down in Foxborough, the focus remains on building up the offensive line to protect our young quarterback. Hearing Mike Vrabel praise rookie tackle Caleb Lomu during OTAs is a nice distraction from the baseball misery. Caleb Lomu has the size and the tools, and getting him ready for the NFL grind is the most important storyline of this offseason. We all know how tough the transition is for young linemen, but the kid needs to be a cornerstone for this offense. Let's hope he keeps progressing, because the future of this franchise depends on keeping Drake Maye upright and healthy.

news_digest.headline: Caleb Lomu receives praise from Mike Vrabel
news_digest.dans_take: It is great to hear Vrabel praising the rookie tackle, because protecting the quarterback is everything.

news_digest.headline: Red Sox visit the Guardians on 3-game road win streak
news_digest.dans_take: We need to carry some of that road magic into Cleveland because this Guardians team is no joke.

news_digest.headline: The pros and cons of the new NBA draft lottery reform
news_digest.dans_take: The league can tweak the lottery all they want, but the Celtics just need to focus on building a championship roster.
